subject: painted fingernails
title: What If You Always Wore Nail Polish?

scenes.text: What if you always wore nail polish? Your nails wouldn't suffocate. Something else gets in.
First, the myth. Nails are dead keratin. They get oxygen from your blood, not the air.
Duke scientists tested 26 women. Within ten to fourteen hours of painting, a polish chemical showed up in their urine.
A breakdown product of triphenyl phosphate jumped nearly seven times. It's a suspected hormone disruptor.
Weeks of dark polish can stain nails yellow. Peel it off and you may see rough white patches.
Those patches are harmless. The real exposure came through the skin, not the nail.

description:
What if you always wore nail polish? Nails don't need to breathe: they are dead keratin fed by the blood.
A 2015 Duke and EWG study of 26 women found a metabolite of triphenyl phosphate in urine rose nearly sevenfold 10 to 14 hours after painting, mostly through the skin. Dark polish can stain nails, which recover over weeks.
